verdict.description: The claim's headline: the most adverse verdict any cited source gave. `not_addressed` means every available cited source was read and none spoke to the claim — distinct from `contradicted` (a source says otherwise) and from `not_retrieved` (no source could be obtained). Per-source detail is in `judgements`.

judgements.description: One entry per AVAILABLE cited source, each judged in its own model call. Absent on results.json written before multi-source checking, where the claim-level fields were the whole answer.

ref.description: The citation label this source answers for, e.g. "3".

unjudged_refs.description: Co-cited labels that could NOT be obtained, so were never opened. The verdict says nothing about these. Sources that WERE available appear in `judgements` instead.

anchor_located.description: False when no anchor phrase was found on the evidence page — the crop exists but carries no red box. null before the highlight step runs.

coverage.description: The deterministic citation audit. The three label-level keys are the original contract and keep their meaning exactly; the occurrence-level keys are additive and NOTHING new is required, so a results.json written before coverage/2 still validates.

covered.description: Labels cited by at least one extracted claim. NOT redefined as 'labels with at least one covered occurrence' — that would push an all-uncertain label into `missing` and silently change a published key.

missing.description: Labels no extracted claim cites. A list of label strings; evals/align.py intersects it to decide whether an unmatched gold case is the tool's failure or the evaluator's.

schema.description: 'coverage/2' when occurrence-level keys are present. Absent means the label-level audit that shipped before them.

source.description: Where occurrences were read from. source_map is authoritative (block, page, heading path); clean.md is the fallback for a case folder with no map and carries neither block nor page.

labels_partially_covered.description: Labels reached by a claim in one place and not in another. A gold case sitting on such an occurrence is an extraction gap, not an alignment failure.

labels_uncertain_only.description: Labels whose every occurrence is `uncertain`: a claim cites the label and the tool cannot say which place it came from.

uncertain.description: Never counted as covered and never as uncovered. A third status, always printed beside the ratio.

id.description: block:offset:label, or clean:offset:label under the clean.md fallback. A group [7,8] yields two occurrences sharing block and offset, distinct by label.

group.description: The bracketed group as printed, e.g. '7,8'.

sentence.description: The sentence carrying the marker, clipped to ±120 chars around it.

attribution.description: How claims were matched to occurrences. Reading-order zipping is deliberately not used: the order is unverified and degrades silently on one skipped claim.

claims_unattributed.description: Claims citing a label that reached no specific occurrence — surplus claims, and claims the attributor refused to place.

truncated.description: Inputs the character limits cut short. Keys are 'manuscript' or 'source:<slug>'; text past the cut was never sent to the model, so it was never checked.
